Methods: We constructed machine learning (ML)-based categorical ASD subtypes and corresponding continuous ASD subtype scores using 14 key clinical symptom measures with adjustment of sex and age among 6,355 autistic children in the Simons Foundation Powering Autism Research for Knowledge (SPARK) cohort by Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction via learning a Tree (DDRTree). We then replicated and validated these subtypes and scores among 2,717 autistic children in the Simons Simplex Collection (SSC) using a modified k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) approach. In SPARK and SSC, we further clinically validated the framework by examining associations of subtype classifications and scores with support needs, service utilization and medication use by regression models with adjustment for sex, age, genetic ancestry and socioeconomic factors. We further assessed SNP-based heritability, cell-type-specific heritability enrichment, polygenic scores (PGS) for psychiatric and cognitive traits, as well as rare copy-number variant (CNV) and de novo variant (DNV) burdens across the ML-derived ASD subtype scores adjusting for sex, age and genetic ancestry. Results: We identified three clinically distinct ASD subtypes in SPARK varying in the types of supports utilized: a high-support-needs (HSN) subtype characterized by broad developmental and functional impairments and very substantial support needs (OR = 1.63, P = 3.71 x 10 -98 ); an emotional-behavioral-support-needs (EBSN) subtype marked by severe repetitive behaviors, elevated psychiatric comorbidity; and a low-support-needs (LSN) subtype with milder symptoms and relatively lower overall support needs. The three groups were associated with differential patterns in the specific types of treatments that were most common for them, from higher intensity to lower intensity. Projected ASD subtypes and scores in SSC recapitulated the phenotypic and medication-use patterns observed in SPARK. SNP-based heritability was highest for the EBSN score (h 2 g = 0.224, SE = 0.051) followed by the HSN (h 2 g = 0.167, SE = 0.049) and LSN score (h 2 g = 0.064, SE = 0.044), with suggestive cell-type-specific heritability enrichments in fetal endodermal cells and adult motor neurons for EBSN score and fetal excitatory neurons and astrocytes for HSN score (both P < 0.05). PGS of ADHD and major depressive disorder were consistently associated with higher EBSN scores in both SPARK and SSC. Higher DNV and rare CNV burden were associated with higher HSN score in SPARK, and higher rare CNV burden was associated with higher EBSN score in SSC (P < 0.05). Conclusions: Our ML-based transferable ASD subtype framework captured clinically and genetically meaningful dimensions of ASD heterogeneity, warranting further validation in larger cohorts. Keywords: Autism spectrum disorder, phenotypic heterogeneity, subtypes, machine learning, genetic burden
n8e981a4ed59d: Malaria transmission models can generate precise intervention rankings even when their parameters, observation mappings and programme costs remain uncertain. I evaluated an age-stratified SEIR-SEI framework in a standardised population of one million, using an unchanged 36-month historical synthetic target. The reconciled implementation maintained virtual age-group totals, fitted the transmission composite K = beta_0 * M, integrated infectious onsets and disease deaths, and compared interventions from one phase-aligned baseline state over 720 days. An aggregate vaccine effect entered child infection before simulation, allowing transmission feedback. Five calibration seeds gave total-series R-squared of 0.9537; subgroup fits were weaker. The closed-form unforced reproduction index, 6.3787, matched the six-state next-generation matrix. The baseline produced 528,041 expected reported episodes. ITN coverage of 50% averted 36,692 episodes; vaccine coverage of 70% averted 2,123 under the assumed aggregate mechanism. At a hypothetical US$2 million additional prevention budget, five allocation seeds and a 10,201-point boundary grid selected 71.43% ITN coverage, averting 52,482.83 reported episodes. The same corner won within a 115-portfolio pool for all 300 assumed parameter draws and remained selected after 40 repeated noisy-target recalibrations. Halving the IRS round price and using two rounds changed the selected mix to 40.07% ITN and 21.95% IRS. All 17 mathematical and numerical assertions passed. The study demonstrates reproducible conditional calculations and identifies important structural confounding. It does not establish empirical Uganda programme effectiveness, a clinical treatment allocation or a national cost-effectiveness recommendation. Empirical use requires compatible surveillance observations, a cohort-based vaccine mechanism, treatment-specific clinical effects and locally measured programme resources.
n5b0ea9a41938: Importance: Preterm birth is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality and disproportionately affects Black birthing people in the United States. DNA methylation based measures of biological aging may capture physiologic dysregulation relevant to birth timing. We aim to determine whether maternal epigenetic age acceleration in early pregnancy is associated with gestational duration, spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB), and small for gestational age (SGA) among Black nulliparous pregnant individuals. Methods: This is a secondary data analysis of the prospective, multicenter Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-Be (nuMoM2b). Participants enrolled in eight US clinical research sites from 2010 to 2014 were followed through delivery; DNAm arrays were processed in 2024, and the current analysis was conducted in 2026. Participants were nulliparous individuals with singleton pregnancies who self-identified as Black. Maternal peripheral blood DNA methylation was measured at 6 to13 weeks of gestation using the Illumina MethylationEPIC array. The primary aging metric was standardized GrimAge2 age acceleration. Principal Components versions of the Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, GrimAge, and DNAmTL clocks, and DunedinPACE, were used in additional analyses. Delivery data was abstracted from medical records in the NuMom2b study. Outcomes were gestational duration in days, based on the best obstetric estimate, adjudicated sPTB before 37 completed weeks, and SGA. Primary linear and logistic regression models adjusted for maternal age, smoking, gestational age at blood draw, and estimated blood cell composition. Secondary models added education and body mass index (BMI) as additional covariates. Fetal sex interaction effects were tested. Results: Among 931 participants (mean age = 23.46 [SD=5.33] years), 55 (5.9%) experienced sPTB. Each 1-SD higher GrimAge2 acceleration was associated with 1.32 fewer days of gestation (b = -1.32 days; 95% CI, -2.36 to -0.28; P=.01) and higher odds of sPTB (odds ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.13-2.02; P=.01). Results were slightly attenuated but remained significant for sPTB when controlling for education and BMI. Epigenetic age acceleration was not associated with SGA. Results were not significantly different by fetal sex. Conclusions and Relevance: Greater first-trimester maternal GrimAge2 acceleration was associated with shorter gestation and 51% higher odds of sPTB but was not associated with SGA among Black nulliparous participants. The association with sPTB persisted after adjustment for socioeconomic and metabolic characteristics, warranting further evaluation of whether GrimAge2 improves early-pregnancy prediction of sPTB value beyond these factors.
nc8ee7c905790: Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) for anxiety symptoms in adults with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). Design: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Data Sources: CINAHL, Embase, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Scopus, SocINDEX, ERIC (EBSCO), and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to October 2025; identified trial protocols were hand-searched for subsequent reports through February 2026. Eligibility criteria for selecting studies: Randomized, non-randomized, and single-arm trials evaluating the effects of MBSR on anxiety in adults with GAD. Data extraction and synthesis: Two authors independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. The primary outcome was anxiety symptoms; the secondary outcome was adverse events. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted, and certainty of evidence was assessed. Results: Of 19 included reports (16 independent samples), 8 randomized controlled trials (n=1,012) were included in the primary meta-analysis. MBSR significantly reduced anxiety symptoms vs. waitlist (Hedges' g=-0.88; 95% CI -1.57 to -0.19) and general active comparators (g=-0.85; 95% CI -1.15 to -0.54), and showed no significant difference vs. escitalopram in two linked trials (g=0.09; 95% CI -0.11 to 0.29), with fewer adverse events in the in-person trial, the only one reporting them (15% vs. 79%; number needed to treat to avoid harm=2). GRADE certainty of evidence was high for the escitalopram comparison and very low for waitlist. Conclusions: MBSR is a well-tolerated, nonpharmacologic treatment option for adults with GAD. Anxiety reductions were similar to escitalopram, with fewer adverse events; independent replication is needed. MBSR may be a viable option for patients who prefer non-pharmacological management or who cannot tolerate medication. Systematic review registration: PROSPERO CRD420251140213.
n90531c7457dd: Endometriosis affects millions of women worldwide. It is linked to severe pain and leads to high socio-economic costs. Endometriosis is characterized by the growth of tissue resembling the endometrium outside the uterus, with the cause still unclear. This study demonstrates how multimodal bioimaging methods can provide new insights into the elemental and molecular processes of endometriosis at the macroscopic level. By using multimodal bioimaging techniques, the role of trace elements (TE) and changes in molecular composition were investigated in human endometriosis biopsies and compared with TE concentrations in serum and peritoneal fluid during the disease. As an element-specific bioimaging technique, laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) was utilized to analyze the TE profile in human biopsies with high sensitivity. Additionally, a quantum cascade laser-based infrared microspectroscopy generated complementary spatial molecular information of the affected tissue. The chemometric processing of the molecular data was made by using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP). To validate the results obtained, TE levels in body fluids were quantified by using ICP-MS and microassays. Our study demonstrates that differences in the TE profile and at the protein level, in terms of mucin expression, can be detected in lesion areas. The TE changes in the tissue differed from those in the body fluids. The presence of mucins in the lesion areas was additionally confirmed by immunohistochemistry. These results highlight the potential of imaging methods in the field of endometriosis research and offer a promising avenue for further studies.
ncdd3999b9f0b: Background Children with FGFR-related craniosynostoses frequently require prolonged nasal continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) for severe obstructive sleep apnea while definitive craniofacial procedures are delayed. We investigated whether sustained CPAP use alters midfacial growth and identified the morphological and biomechanical determinants of this effect. Methods In this retrospective observational study, we combined longitudinal 3D morphometric analyses of craniofacial shape in CPAP-treated and untreated children with FGFR-related craniosynostoses with experimental measurements of mask-induced forces and pressure distribution using 3D-printed patient-specific facial models instrumented with sensors. Multivariate analyses characterized growth trajectories, and structural equation modeling (SEM) disentangled the effects of three major risk factors: age, initial morphology, and CPAP duration. Results CPAP-treated patients exhibited a distinct growth trajectory characterized by greater midfacial retrusion than untreated patients with similar baseline morphology. Mask use generated mechanical loads of 6-10 N. Intentional overtightening markedly increased the total force applied to the face, but no notable difference was observed between expert and non-expert operators. Craniofacial morphology was the main determinant of force and pressure distributions and of growth response, identifying morphological risk factors. CPAP duration exaggerated these effects, particularly at younger ages. SEM supported links between morphology, mechanical loading, and deviation from expected growth. Conclusions Nasal CPAP is associated with additional midfacial growth deviation in children with FGFR-related craniosynostoses, with susceptibility strongly dependent on baseline morphology, treatment duration, and age at initiation. These findings support systematic craniofacial growth monitoring during prolonged CPAP and consideration of respiratory management and interface fit within longitudinal craniofacial treatment planning.
n777a459425b3: Background: Childhood overweight is often expected to emerge first among urban and wealthier populations during the nutrition transition. However, evidence on temporal trends in childhood overweight and the independent contributions of household wealth and urban residence in Bangladesh remains limited. Methods: We analysed data from 63,972 children aged 0-59 months with valid weight-for-height z-scores (WHZ) from the Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS) of 2012-13, 2019 and 2025. Overweight was defined as WHZ >+2 according to the 2006 WHO Child Growth Standards. We estimated survey-weighted prevalence, absolute and relative wealth inequalities, and prevalence ratios for urban versus rural residence using regression models adjusted for household wealth and other measured characteristics. We also assessed anthropometric data quality and conducted sensitivity analyses. Results: National overweight prevalence was 1.6% (95% CI 1.4-1.9) in 2012-13, 2.4% (2.2-2.7) in 2019 and 1.7% (1.5-2.0) in 2025. The 2019 peak was concentrated in urban Dhaka district, where one measurer recorded all 67 overweight cases and WHZ variability was high. Excluding this area, prevalence was 1.5%, 1.9% and 1.7%, respectively. The fully adjusted relative index of inequality for wealth remained similar across surveys: 3.66 (1.93-6.93), 3.55 (2.21-5.71) and 3.35 (2.02-5.54), with no evidence of temporal change (interaction p=0.974). The wealth-adjusted urban-to-rural prevalence ratio was 1.44 (1.01-2.06) in 2012-13 and 1.77 (1.40-2.24) in 2019, then fell to 0.72 (0.54-0.95) in 2025. Mean WHZ decreased by 0.16 (95% CI-0.19 to -0.13) between 2019 and 2025, while wasting prevalence increased from 9.8% to 12.9%. In 2025, 41.4% (35.3-47.7) of overweight children were also stunted. Conclusions: Childhood overweight showed no sustained national increase, but persistent wealth inequalities remained. The changing association with urban residence and concerns about measurement quality highlight the need for continued surveillance and stronger anthropometric quality assurance.
nf3a7808f6d98: Parental history of dementia is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease, although the mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. We hypothesize that differences in epigenetic aging may contribute to this increased risk. We examined DNA methylation (DNAm)-based measures of epigenetic aging, telomere length, immune cell composition, and MRI-based measures of brain aging in 1,204 middle-aged adults. Parental dementia history was not associated with accelerated epigenetic or brain aging. However, it was associated with CD8 memory T cell expansion, with nominal differences in CD4 memory T cells, memory B cells, and telomere length. The association with shorter telomere length was attenuated after accounting for CD8 memory T cells, supporting a CD8-specific relationship. Earlier parental dementia onset was associated with faster pace of biological aging, while poorer parental cognitive performance was associated with lower naive and higher memory immune cell proportions, accelerated epigenetic aging, and a larger brain age gap. These findings suggest that midlife adults with parental dementia history exhibit a peripheral immune aging signature characterized by a naive-to-memory T cell shift. Parental cognitive performance was also associated with accelerated epigenetic aging and brain age gap, suggesting that familial dementia risk is reflected across multiple aging dimensions in midlife offspring.
nb8d5ae9bce5d: Vascular pathology often manifests in complex shape evolution visualized by longitudinal computed tomography (CT) imaging. Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing. While existing shell growth formulations can mitigate this burden, they require nontrivial FE implementation especially in commercial softwares (e.g., Abaqus) and their efficacy in patient-specific geometries under complex loading is unclear. In this work, we present a general computational framework to implement shell morphoelastic growth computed directly from registered patient-specific CT images. This shell implementation is validated against solid 3D formulations, allows thickness tunability, and increases compatibility with CT surfaces. We demonstrate the robustness of this formulation through modeling post-operative growth in a patient-specific aortic dissection under stent-based loading. Results first show that complex stent-based loading can deform the shell dissection flap to reproduce post-operative geometry. The outer aortic wall is then given a growth field calculated from registration of 1-month and 5-year post-operative CT images, which is implemented along with stent-based loading and pressurization. Results from this model capture the trends in total and lumen morphological evolution observed at intermediate timepoints. These findings establish a general framework, validated with a patient-specific case study of aortic dissection, with the potential to expand to other complex systems, scale to larger patient populations, and apply G&R to clinical translation.
n5dcc9b334709: Importance: Blood based proteomic biomarkers may support scalable dementia research, but their associations with cognitive phenotype remain poorly characterized in sub Saharan African populations. Objective: To examine associations between selected plasma proteins and multidomain cognitive performance in older adults in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Design: Cross sectional secondary analysis of baseline data from the Etude du Vieillissement Cognitif et de Demence en Republique Democratique du Congo (EVCD RDC), with participant recruitment and data collection from July 2024 through September 2025. Setting: Community based prospective cohort in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Participants: The analytic sample included 779 participants: 143 cognitively unimpaired, 218 with mild cognitive impairment, 203 with Alzheimer disease, and 215 with other dementia. Median age was 73 years (IQR, 70 to 78); 495 participants (63.5%) were female and 284 (36.5%) were male. Exposures: Plasma abundance of 10 candidate proteins measured using the NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel 120. Candidates were selected from an earlier panel wide analysis based on cognitively unimpaired vs Alzheimer disease discrimination and false discovery rate adjusted significance. Main Outcomes and Measures: Seven cognitive outcomes spanning global cognition, language, working memory, learning, delayed memory, mental abstraction, and problem solving. Separate linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, current smoking, education, and estimated glomerular filtration rate. Benjamini Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied within each cognitive outcome across the 10 proteins. Results: Eighteen protein cognition associations were nominally significant, and 6 remained significant after correction. Higher MME was associated with better language, global cognition, and delayed memory. Higher NEFL was associated with poorer global cognition and delayed memory. Higher ENO2 was associated with better delayed memory. No p tau217 based measure remained significant after correction. Conclusions and Relevance: MME and NEFL showed the most consistent associations with cognitive performance, whereas ptau217 based measures did not survive multiple testing correction. Biomarkers optimized for Alzheimer pathology detection may differ from those most closely associated with cross sectional cognitive phenotype, supporting population specific evaluation of plasma proteomic markers.
n0029080f69fb: Importance: Plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration may help characterise progression across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum. Plasma eMTBR-tau243 has been associated with tau pathology and cognitive decline. Whether plasma eMTBR-tau levels differ across subjective cognitive decline (SCD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD dementia, between MCI subtypes, or best discriminate subsequent clinical progression in brain health and memory clinic populations remains unclear. Objective: To compare plasma eMTBR-tau and selected biomarkers of neurodegeneration, neuropathology, and neuroinflammation across the AD continuum by pTau217 and APOE {epsilon}4 status, and explore their associations with clinical progression over two years. Design: Observational cohort study with longitudinal follow-up in a subset of participants. Setting: Healthy Brain Ageing (HBA) brain health and memory clinic, Sydney, Australia. Participants underwent assessment between October 2018 and April 2026. Participants: Cross-sectional analysis included 436 participants; 166 were followed up approximately two years later. Exposures: Plasma biomarker quantification using the NULISAseq Neuro 220 Panel, clinical classification by multidisciplinary memory clinic assessment, plasma pTau217 status (SIMOA ALZpath), and APOE {epsilon}4 carrier status. Main Outcomes and Measures: Fasting blood was collected on the morning of assessment. Plasma was analysed using the NULISAseq Neuro 220 panel. Relative biomarker abundance was compared across clinical and biomarker-defined groups. BD-pTau217 and eMTBR-tau levels at the preceding assessment were modelled individually and jointly to assess SCD-to-MCI progression and MCI-to-AD conversion over approximately two years of follow-up. Results: Among 436 participants (mean [SD] age, 70.2 [8.0] years; 67.2% female), 186 had SCD, 228 MCI, and 22 AD dementia. Among 221 biomarkers, phosphorylated tau analytes (pTau181/T205/T212/217/231) dominated clinical group differences, while eMTBR-tau showed the largest adjusted differences: 1.69-fold higher in MCI than SCD, 6.55-fold higher in AD than SCD and 3.88-fold higher in AD than MCI (all FDR-adjusted P < .001). eMTBR-tau was higher in multidomain amnestic MCI than in SCD, and in pTau217-positive than in pTau217-negative individuals. In the exploratory MCI-to-AD analysis (6/40 converted over 2 years), eMTBR-tau at the preceding assessment showed higher cross-validated discrimination of MCI-to-AD conversion than BD-pTau217 (AUC, 0.936 vs. 0.882). Conclusions and Relevance: Clinical stages across the AD continuum are defined by a tau-dominant pattern. eMTBR-tau showed prominent stage-related differences, supporting its further evaluation as a marker of clinical progression.
n76adf5bc2adb: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) comprises three prognostically distinct molecular subtypes: human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated, HPV-independent/p53-wildtype, and HPV-independent/p53-abnormal. Classification requires p16/p53 immunohistochemistry, which consumes tissue and is often incomplete in retrospective cohorts. We investigated whether deep learning could predict HPV/p16 status and molecular subtypes directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images. Using features extracted with H-optimus-1, we developed two attention-based multiple-instance learning models: HERA, predicting HPV/p16 status, and HERMES, predicting the three molecular subtypes. Models were developed on 644 patients from three Dutch VSCC cohorts and tested on 286 patients from two independent cohorts. In independent testing, HERA achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.84 (95% CI 0.75-0.91), with specificity 0.93, negative predictive value 0.94, and sensitivity 0.68. HERA-predicted groups reproduced the prognostic separation of HPV testing (log-rank p<0.001). HERMES achieved a macro-average AUC of 0.70 (0.66-0.75), with good discrimination for HPV-associated (0.80) but limited separation of HPV-independent/p53-abnormal (AUC 0.68) and HPV-independent/p53-wildtype (AUC 0.63). HERMES-predicted classes reproduced the prognostic hierarchy, with 5-year recurrence rates of 14.0% (HPV-associated), 31.1% (HPV-independent/p53-wildtype) and 43.3% (HPV-independent/p53-abnormal) (p=0.0051). Highly attended tiles showed basaloid cells and koilocytotic-like atypia in HPV-associated tumors, keratinizing nests with desmoplastic stroma in HPV-independent/p53-abnormal tumors, and well-differentiated keratinocytes with spongiosis in HPV-independent/p53-wildtype tumors. HERA could assign HPV/p16 status to large retrospective VSCC cohorts lacking ancillary testing, without consuming tissue, enabling HPV-stratified outcome analyses. Before such use, external validation of its discrimination and calibration across scanners and populations is required. HERMES suggests that molecular subtype information is encoded in hematoxylin and eosin-stained slides, but requires improved distinction between the HPV-independent subtypes.
n20d398c495bc: Primaquine is currently the only widely available antimalarial drug that targets mature \emph{Plasmodium falciparum} gametocytes, the life stage in the human bloodstream that mediates transmission from humans to mosquitoes. The only study that provided large-scale field data suitable for examining the additional impact of the WHO-recommended dose of 0.25 mg/kg primaquine in an artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT)-based mass drug administration (MDA) campaign was reported by Deng et al. (2018, Clinical Infectious Diseases). The study showed that both ACT alone and ACT plus primaquine substantially reduced average monthly malaria hospital rates and the prevalence of infection after the MDA campaign but no additional benefit was observed with primaquine. These findings challenge our expectations for the population-level impacts of primaquine and are in stark contrast to the predictions (of substantial population-level impacts) made by existing epidemiological-scale modelling studies. To address these knowledge gaps, we hypothesised that individuals' adherence patterns to multi-round MDA campaigns could be a factor that explains these conflicting empirical observations. To examine this hypothesis, we developed a data-driven multiscale agent-based model of malaria infection and transmission, which quantitatively captures both the detailed biology of human infection kinetics and the pharmacodynamic actions of antimalarial drugs. Our model provides a coherent explanation for these apparently disparate observations, including the individual-level gametocytocidal effect of primaquine, the population-level impacts of primaquine in MDA campaigns, and the population-level impacts predicted by previous modelling studies. All three observations can be explained by underlying adherence patterns within a single modelling framework. We used our model to predict the effect of primaquine in routine case management outside MDA, finding that administration could significantly reduce the prevalence of infection, supporting its use as a transmission-blocking intervention against malaria.
n68b4978fabc4: Background Unspecified psychosis-spectrum diagnoses (ICD code F29) are commonly used when the underlying disorder remains uncertain, particularly at first presentation. These diagnoses may persist or later be revised as the clinical picture evolves, yet little is known about their long-term trajectories or implications for treatment and service use in routine mental healthcare. Objectives To describe the usage and persistence of unspecified non-organic psychosis (F29) and other non-specific diagnoses, and the time to transition to a specific diagnosis. Secondary objectives are to describe temporal trends in their use, identify demographic and clinical characteristics associated with diagnostic persistence, and characterise treatment patterns, service utilisation, mortality, and discharge across diagnostic groups. Methods We will conduct a retrospective longitudinal cohort study using de-identified electronic health-record data from the South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust (SLaM), accessed through the Clinical Record Interactive Search (CRIS) system, between 1 January 2007 and 31 December 2024. The study population will include patients with an ICD-10 psychosis-spectrum diagnosis (F2x.x), substance induced psychotic disorder (or F1x.5), bipolar disorder or affective disorder with documented psychotic symptoms(F32/3.3). Diagnoses will be classified as specific or non-specific according to their ICD-10 category. Primary analysis will examine time from first F29 diagnosis to first subsequent specific psychosis-spectrum or bipolar diagnosis using Cox proportional hazards regression, with discharge from SLaM, death and administrative end of follow-up treated as censoring events. Associations with diagnostic transition will be examined adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, area-level deprivation, route of service entry, and calendar period. Secondary competing-risk analysis will estimate the cumulative incidence of diagnostic transition using the Aalen Johansen estimator, treating discharge and death as competing events. Ethics and Dissemination CRIS operates under ethical approval from the South Central Oxford C Research Ethics Committee (23/SC/0257). Project-specific approval was received from the CRIS Oversight Committee as Project 23 095. The study will be reported in accordance with the RECORD extension of the STROBE guidelines. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and will provide evidence on the longitudinal use and refinement of non-specific psychosis-spectrum diagnoses in routine secondary mental healthcare.
ndb6d7ccc9364: Purpose This study explored the contribution of a Forensic Service for adult safeguarding introduced in one geographic area. This service introduced the role of Forensic Medical Examiner (FME) to examine and interpret injuries when there are concerns that these may have non-accidental causes. This paper explores the perspectives of adult safeguarding Social Workers and the FME about their experiences of the service and how it supported their decision-making and safeguarding practice. Methodology Semi-structured interviews were conducted with the FME and Social Workers from safeguarding adults teams. The data was analysed using thematic analysis. Findings Four themes were generated through the analysis. These highlighted the challenges for Social Workers and other practitioners in identifying whether a non-accidental injury has occurred; the role of forensic information in enhancing knowledge and understanding; the contribution of forensic information to safeguarding decision making and activity; Social Worker and FME experiences of working together within the new service. Originality The Forensic Service is, to the best of our understanding, the first service of its kind within the United Kingdom. It appears to represent a unique response to the challenges of interpreting injuries and determining when these may be non-accidental, and attributable to physical abuse or neglect.
n56fc0887b88f: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal. We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously-observed "Slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's $ε$ hyperparameter.
nc162796d35c4: Understanding and controlling how systems evolve is central to science and engineering, where many problems require reasoning about complete trajectories. Existing approaches typically learn local dynamics or generate trajectories, but objectives constructed from individual transitions can miss dependencies across time, while generative models do not necessarily provide a tractable objective for evaluating and optimizing arbitrary paths. We study $\textit{action learning}$, the problem of recovering a stochastic action from trajectory observations, yielding a common objective for reasoning about dynamical systems. We introduce $\textbf{LEAP}$ ($\textbf{L}$earned $\textbf{E}$nergy on $\textbf{A}$ction $\textbf{P}$aths), which anchors the unknown action to a tractable reference process and learns the remaining correction by comparing observed trajectories with reference trajectories. This construction yields a differentiable objective on path space that can capture both local dynamical structure and nonadditive dependencies across time. Once learned, the same action can be flexibly reused for path ranking and inference, mechanism steering, constrained optimization and sampling. Across stochastic physical systems, many-body orbital dynamics and molecular simulations, LEAP recovers underlying dynamics, captures dependencies across time and enables transfer across inference objectives and physical conditions. We show that $\textit{action learning}$ is a promising framework for turning trajectory observations into reusable objectives for scientific inference and control.
n185e5affa18f: Knowledge graph-to-text (KG-to-text) generation verbalizes a set of knowledge graph triples into fluent natural language. While fine-tuned encoder-decoder models have long been the standard approach, recent LLMs are becoming increasingly competitive. We benchmark recent LLMs against fine-tuned encoder-decoder models, using reference-based metrics and graph-grounded reference-free LLM-based evaluation validated against human annotations. We observed that recent LLMs substantially narrow, and in several settings close, the gap with fine-tuned models on reference-based metrics, while performing better on graph-grounded metrics. LLM-based evaluation scores show limited correlation with reference-based metrics, suggesting that the two approaches capture different aspects of generation quality. Graph-grounded evaluation reveals that prompted models produce fewer contradictions and triple omissions than fine-tuned models, and these errors increase more rapidly with graph size for fine-tuned models, highlighting differences between the two approaches that reference-based metrics may not fully capture.
n6dbfb04044f4: Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers. During inference, each recurrence generates independent KV-caches, causing memory to grow linearly. To address this challenge, prior work has proposed KV-sharing (i.e., sharing KV-caches across depth), finding that, in some cases, the KV-cache of the final recurrence can be shared with the earlier recurrences without quality loss, a property we denote as KV-shareability. However, the mechanisms underlying KV-shareability remain poorly understood, with even identically trained looped architectures not consistently exhibiting it. In this paper, we study how KV-shareability can be enabled in looped models. We propose a two-stage method: in the first stage, we use stochastic depth during pretraining, which induces contractive residual dynamics that drive representations toward a common limit across recurrences. In the second stage, we propose BeNice!, a post-training method that broadcasts the final recurrence's KV-cache into the first recurrence, training it to produce compatible residuals while preserving the original model's quality. As a result, BeNice! enables KV-shareability while matching standard finetuning's unshared validation perplexity. Using BeNice!, we show that KV-sharing is complementary to alternative KV-compression methods, composing with memory-efficient sequence mixers (e.g., multi-latent attention, Kimi delta attention) and low-precision KV-cache quantization (e.g., fp8, mxfp8, nvfp4). Finally, in simulated low-memory, long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.
n4aaa006307e1: Diffusion models have become strong priors for solving inverse problems. However, nonlinear inverse problems such as phase retrieval remain challenging when multiple measurement-consistent solutions are distinguishable only by the prior; we call such measurements ambiguous. Existing diffusion-based samplers rely on local approximations during reconstruction. For an ambiguous measurement, these approximations can allow measurement guidance to favor a measurement-consistent mode that is close to a prior-supported mode but is itself not supported by the prior. Evaluation often masks this type of failure by reporting the best-of-$k$ runs, where the best is selected by comparison to the ground truth. We introduce Prior-Consistent DAPS (PC-DAPS), a variant of Decoupled Annealing Posterior Sampling (DAPS) designed to address this failure case by maintaining multiple candidate solutions within a single sampling run. As annealing noise decreases, PC-DAPS prunes and replaces weaker candidates according to their prior consistency, without any ground-truth access. PC-DAPS reduces the incidence of prior-inconsistent samples and improves sample quality on nonlinear inverse problems while preserving sample quality and diversity on linear inverse problems.
n334261bef42a: Hidden future-token leakage can create false architectural gains: an autoregressive model may appear substantially better under teacher-forced evaluation while its free-running generation deteriorates. We investigate this failure in an adaptive residual-routing decoder whose sequence-level routing summary exposes prefix positions to future tokens despite a correct causal attention mask. An anomalous 24-layer checkpoint reduces validation loss from the baseline's 3.5958 to 1.4259, yet it fails a prefix-invariance audit and has substantially higher reference-model perplexity during generation. Layer-wise diagnostics and implementation inspection trace the violation to a full-sequence summary broadcast through the dynamic routing-query path. Two independently trained 12-layer causal repairs eliminate detectable leakage and return validation loss and reference perplexity to the control scale, removing the large apparent advantage. As diagnostic tools, we use the established prefix-invariance contract, maximum prefix-output discrepancy (LeakScore), complementary behavioral metrics, and layer-wise profiles. Supporting experiments cover six synthetic implementation pairs spanning five module families, clean pretrained controls, controlled fault injection, and cache consistency across numerical precisions. These results illustrate how hidden future-token access can produce misleading claims of architectural progress and why lower teacher-forced loss should be interpreted together with whole-model causal checks and free-running evaluation.
n3d51169ff705: While monolingual language model (LM) surprisal is widely established as a predictor of reading times, it cannot capture the non-native (L2) reading dynamics that are shaped by the reader's first language (L1). In this work, we investigate whether the cross-lingual transfer within bilingual models aligns with human L1-driven biases during L2 reading. We evaluate bilingual models on eye-tracking data of readers from 12 diverse L1 backgrounds reading English texts. To isolate L1-specific transfer, we compare bilingual models trained on an L1 that matches the readers' L1 background to both a monolingual English baseline and bilingual models trained on other L1s. We demonstrate that matching the readers' L1 improves the prediction of L2 reading times. This predictive advantage is concentrated in late-stage eye-tracking measures, modulated by L1-L2 script overlap, and peaks among intermediate-proficiency readers. These findings provide evidence that bilingual LMs capture aspects of cross-linguistic influence, and that such influence is present in L2 reading behavior.
n78cd3defd644: Counterfactual explanation methods have been introduced for unimodal settings, with dedicated frameworks for tabular, timeseries, text, and image data, yet no post-hoc method has been designed for classifiers that learn from multimodal inputs. Existing explainability methods for multimodal classifiers apply modality-specific attribution independently to each input, which fails to yield coherent explanations and does not transfer to arbitrary pre-trained multimodal architectures. To address these shortcomings, we present CRANE (Counterfactual Retrieval via Agnostic Nearest-neighbour Explanations), the first post-hoc, model-agnostic framework for nearest-neighbour multimodal counterfactual generation that retrieves real training examples from the target class as candidate explanations, ensuring plausibility by construction. Across four heterogeneous datasets and three fusion strategies, we show that Multimodal Consensus Retrieval (MC-R), which intersects per-modality neighbour sets to identify instances jointly close to the query in every modality, emerges as the strongest multimodal strategy, achieving the best or joint-best outcome on three of four datasets while grounding every explanation in the joint training distribution. Unimodal strategies remain competitive when a single modality dominates the decision boundary.
n7a7c6d8337b4: Multilingual pipelines such as FineWeb2 apply one recipe across a thousand languages, leaving the failure modes of individual languages unanticipated. We use an LLM once, as a corpus debugger rather than a classifier: a tool-using agent explores the corpus through a read-only, budgeted API and compiles each finding into an executable test, which a native speaker then validates. On the 26.5M-document Slovak portion of FineWeb2, three runs costing \$2.21-\$2.84 each found seven findings over four phenomena. The largest is a machine-generated content farm of 1,408,437 documents (5.32%) that passed the pipeline's filters, 86.6% of it passing even stricter thresholds. Blinded labels support 6 of the 7 findings (defect rates .53-1.00 against .08 in a random control) and do not support one. The compiled suite scans the full corpus in 0.7 s of wall-clock time without a GPU, against \$12k-\$90k per LLM classification pass. The best static sampling baseline validates more selectors than any agent run, at under half the cost. The agent contributes exact prevalence, a precision estimate checked against sampled documents, an account of why the pipeline missed each slice, and a reusable test. We release the framework, Slovak test suite, validation data and agent trajectories.
nc2eb6f045a98: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits step-by-step rationales that appear to explain model predictions, but there is no guarantee these steps causally drive the final answer. In standard autoregressive generation, dense attention allows each reasoning step to attend to the full context, enabling the model to derive answers through direct lookup while generating plausible-sounding but post-hoc justifications. We introduce CausalCoT, an inference framework that enforces causal transparency by decomposing problems into a directed acyclic graph of atomic sub-questions, evaluating each node in an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents. This Markovian structure removes attention pathways to non-parent content, making downstream predictions sensitive to local reasoning rather than global context leakage. Across a diverse suite of reasoning benchmarks, CausalCoT preserves competitive predictive performance while improving explanation faithfulness, increasing causal sensitivity of intermediate reasoning steps by an average of 12 and up to 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline. The structured dependency graph additionally enables test-time interventions in which local corrections propagate predictably through downstream reasoning.
n52ee08f4be7a: Industrial organizations hold operational knowledge in structured records, such as telemetry, point lists, and transactions, and in unstructured sources, such as manuals, service notes, communications, and inspection reports. Governance programs often manage these sources separately. Classifying, linking, and documenting them depends on a small group of employees with deep domain knowledge. Agents built on large language models can propose metadata, cite documents, and flag quality issues, but unreviewed proposals can spread errors into downstream systems. A perfunctory approval leaves no record of what a reviewer checked. We present contestable governance: specialist agents produce scored, cited arguments for disputed metadata decisions; a steward can accept, reject, modify, or add arguments before commit; and a governance record retains the evidence, interventions, and outcome. A versioned domain glossary supplies model-specific terms and acronym definitions to the agents. We describe the workflow, a triage path that reserves full argumentation for uncertain proposals while preserving review before commit, the scoring and record models, and a gate that controls which verified decisions become precedent. Two HVAC use cases illustrate the pattern: point classification using Brick Schema class labels, supported by an open reference implementation, and an illustrative warranty failure-mode decision linking claim fields and telemetry to service notes and revisioned bulletins.
nc2ca7e391af4: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.
n2bb09387dffd: \emph{Continuous-space} attacks find prompts that trigger malicious behaviors, such as overthinking, in black-box LLMs by sampling or optimizing over a low-dimensional Gaussian latent space and decoding it to text through a \emph{random mapping} and nearest-token lookup. Because the random mapping is not learned from language, its prompts can be highly unnatural, and as such easily detectable through input guardrails, and the risk estimates they yield are not grounded in natural prompts. In this paper, we demonstrate that the same continuous latent-space framework can be coupled directly to a learned generative distribution over language, a continuous diffusion language model (dLLM), which removes the artificial random mapping while preserving the standard-Gaussian latent formulation and the downstream sampling or optimization procedure. We evaluate this approach under two settings: sampling-based estimation using \emph{RareTrap} and optimization-based search using \emph{ThinkTrap}. We find that character-level perplexity drops from $10^3$--$10^7$ to 3--5 in RareTrap and from 20--28 to 4.3--5.4 in ThinkTrap. We also find that model risk estimates can differ by an order of magnitude across the two mappings.
n10479997ddbc: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training. By casting the values and derivatives at the query and neighbouring samples as latent variables in a constrained optimisation problem, the burden of long training loops becomes one of on-demand local solves. We establish Diona's theoretical properties including finite-sample coverage and, in the noiseless case, convergence to the true state and derivatives under dense sampling. In a nonlinear regression benchmark on six functions of three to eight dimensions, Diona was more accurate than a Gaussian process (GP) on noiseless data especially with denser data sets. Furthermore, as with GP, it produced uncertainty bounds that contained the true value at more than 95% of query points in four functions. Diona's time to a first prediction after a data set update was three to four orders of magnitude shorter than that of the GP, and two to three orders shorter than that of a neural network, which was more accurate but offers no uncertainty quantification. This low latency is paid for by on-demand predictions, so this latency advantage applies when relatively few predictions are needed between data updates.
ndb8edc4e6bbb: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.
nefe3f0c440bd: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.
n5ea2658a9713: We study learning a discrete distribution under person-level differential privacy in the batched setting. Given $n$ users, each contributing $m$ i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution $μ$ over $[k]$, we seek an estimate of $μ$ with total-variation error $α$. We give polynomial-time algorithms under both pure and approximate differential privacy. Under pure $(\varepsilon,0)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(α^2 m)+k/(α\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k/\varepsilon)$, the first polynomial-time pure-DP guarantee matching the information-theoretic optimum up to logarithmic factors. Under approximate $(\varepsilon,δ)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(α^2 m)+k/(α\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k+\log(1/δ)/\varepsilon)$. At $δ=2^{-Θ(k)}$, this is $\widetilde O(k)$ for fixed $α,\varepsilon,m$ and failure probability. Our algorithms use a new degree-6 sum-of-squares estimator for learning from untrusted batches. Its key ingredient is a trace-bounded diagonal majorizer for the difference between the empirical covariance of the repaired batch averages and the multinomial covariance predicted by their mean. We prove that clean data admit this certificate through semidefinite-programming duality and a new application of the stronger symmetric form of Grothendieck's inequality due to Friedland and Lim. The certificate preserves the mean-dependent variance of multinomial batch averages, yielding the near-optimal robust rate $O(η\sqrt{\log(1/η)/m})$ and providing the score required by the privacy reduction. We also prove a statistical query lower bound ruling out a uniformly smaller order of error under fixed polynomial SQ resource bounds.
n58751d238db5: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true. We introduce \bench{}, an executable benchmark for evaluating unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery in LLM agents under missing evidence. It contains 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains. By systematically suppressing critical facts, the benchmark measures unsafe execution under critical evidence omission and determines the minimum observed failure cardinality, including failures with full evidence and cases with no observed failure after exhaustive testing. An independent audit tool tests whether agents seek missing facts and then withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks. The benchmark reveals substantial variation across the ten models in omission robustness, evidence acquisition, and appropriate action. Resistance to missing evidence does not necessarily translate into useful recovery. Recovery access reduces unsafe execution for all ten models, but agents differ in whether they actively obtain the missing facts and use them to act appropriately in both worlds.
ned4c4556d68c: Recommender systems typically serve one user at a time. However, in households, members share a finite pantry and follow different dietary rules, making independent recommendations prone to resource conflicts and dietary violations. We formulate household food recommendation as constrained fair division and present FairFRESH, a neuro-symbolic framework that learns per-member utilities, allocates foods under explicit welfare objectives, enforces dietary rules through a deterministic filter, and explains recommendations using Shapley and Banzhaf attributions. Theoretically, we show that no finite penalty guarantees compliance near a dietary-rule threshold, establish approximation guarantees for greedy allocation under utilitarian and smoothed Nash objectives in the stock-free model before filtering, and characterize the scale invariance of Nash welfare. We also use the minimax theorem to analyze rotating shared meals. On NHANES-derived data, the learned utility model achieves Recall@20 of 0.293, outperforming five learned recommenders (at most 0.244) but not a previous-day repetition heuristic (0.321). On held-out four-person households, Nash allocation reduces Gini disparity by 42% relative to conflict resolution while improving Recall@20 from 0.180 to 0.197. It comes within 2% of an upper bound on the smoothed Nash optimum, and rescaling one member's utilities changes at most 1.5% of assignments. All recommendations satisfy the encoded dietary rules, while attribution scores correlate with utility loss upon component removal (r = 0.76). In simulation, shared meals reduce pantry use by about one-third, and weekly rotation increases the worst-off member's utility by 38% over the best fixed meal.
ncf32cc301b7e: Understanding catastrophic forgetting, in which learning new tasks degrades performance on previously learned tasks, remains a fundamental challenge in continual learning (CL). Existing theoretical analyses often rely on specific model or task structures and offer limited insight into how iterative optimization affects forgetting. To address this gap, we develop an algorithmic stability framework for expected population forgetting under SGD without prescribing a particular model architecture. Specifically, we decompose forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps and empirical forgetting. To bound the generalization gaps, we track how a sample perturbation affects updates within a task and propagates through subsequent tasks. We consider constant, intra-task decaying, and continuously decaying learning-rate schedules. Comparing the two decaying schedules allows us to characterize how restarting learning-rate decay at task boundaries affects the propagation of historical sample perturbations. For empirical forgetting, we derive bounds for all three schedules by retaining cumulative gradient alignment along the optimization trajectory, without requiring convexity. Combining these results yields upper bounds on expected forgetting that capture the effects of training set size, the number of updates per task, the total number of tasks, learning-rate schedules, and cumulative gradient alignment. Finally, we conduct experiments on Split CIFAR-100 and Split MiniImageNet to examine the empirical implications of our theoretical findings.
ne779ea9623dc: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate domain-specific commercial & medical content (e.g., claims, statements, and promotional phrases) in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals. However, ensuring its regulatory compliance, factual accuracy, and audience-specific personalization remains a major challenge. We report a production case study asking whether moving compliance and personalization signal from prompt-level rules into retrieval time structured context improves pharmaceutical claims generation, using Composer, a deployed internal tool built on a Golden Data Model (GDM) of 1,867 pharmaceutical claims spanning four products. The GDM integrates claim metadata, references, audience labels, material type, usage history, Match Text Variant (MTV) links, and a six dimension quality score (6C). Across six product-audience segments, the context pipeline improves intended indication (+29%), intended content type (+62%) and intended target audience (+67%), 6C quality score (+86%), and claim reuse (+34%). Production log analysis over the deployment period shows a 29.5% reduction in weekly API cost. We report this as descriptive deployment evidence. This work is a systems and data architecture contribution: it shows that in a regulated, high-stakes domain, restructuring claim data for retrieval-time filtering is a more scalable lever than expanding prompt-level rules, and documents the engineering path data cleaning, graph linking, and quality scoring.
n54232631b23f: Purpose: To describe an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol for a clinical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system over breast lesion management literature, addressing the dependence of retrieval scores on annotation coverage. Methods: An 18-document corpus and an 18-query development benchmark, with one Yes/No or WH-question per document, were used. Retrieval combined dense embeddings, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking. Chunk sizes of 128 to 1024 tokens, overlaps of 0 to 20%, and four retriever configurations were evaluated. Relevance was defined by evidence spans mapped to all containing chunks, treating overlapping chunks with equivalent evidence as relevant. Retrieval was evaluated using R-Precision, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG@K. Separately, generation was assessed on a 512-token index at K=1 to 5 using DeepEval claim-level metrics, with deepseek-v4-pro as the LLM judge, and BLEU/ROUGE metrics. Results: The selected hybrid retriever, using 384-token chunks and 20% overlap, retrieved accepted evidence in the top three results for 17 of 18 queries. Recall@3, R-Precision, MRR@3, and nDCG@3 each reached 0.94. Ground-truth curation increased evidence spans from 25 to 37 and accepted chunk targets from 36 to 51 without changing retrieval rankings. Conclusion: Cross-encoder reranking achieved the highest retrieval scores. Expanded relevance annotations increased recognized evidence without changing rankings, highlighting annotation sensitivity. The small development set and retrieval-informed curation require independent validation, including radiologist assessment of evidence sufficiency.
n52bca9f08994: Individual preferences often become visible only after deployment, when a user accepts one decision or revokes it in favor of another. Jev-style typed interfaces make this feedback explicit by identifying the selected action and, under revocation, the decision it replaces. We study how these consequences persist across requests as Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback (Jev-DLC). Jev-DLC treats each correction as both evidence about a recurring action identity and a directed relation between the preferred and rejected choices. It preserves these signals in complementary bounded channels above a frozen scorer and combines their scores to shape the next decision. The method retains no raw interaction history, adds no scorer call, and performs no runtime language-model backward pass. We also introduce TCPA-Bench, a chronological suite that credits a correction only through its effect on later decisions. On TCPA-Repeat, Jev-DLC reaches 44.83% user-macro accuracy overall, 2.43 points above Recent-4 history replay. After at least two earlier feedback events, it reaches 56.07%, a 7.54-point margin over the strongest reported comparison at this depth. These results show how explicit typed corrections can become compact causal state for continual personalization.
n528dae89320c: Local anomaly detection is the task of identifying spatially confined anomalous or out-of-distribution (OOD) regions within an otherwise in-distribution (ID) image. Most existing methods are designed for a specific context, with a strong focus on industrial defect detection, where they achieve excellent performance on well-established benchmarks. However, we observe that these methods can exhibit significant performance drops in other contexts, especially when the inlier distribution is multimodal. To account for this inlier complexity, we propose LACToS, a principled local OOD detection method based on statistical typicality and made tractable through two innovations: (i) grouping pixels into superpixels and (ii) using a computationally efficient proxy to estimate typicality. The code is released here: https://github.com/voilalab/LACToS.
n4a6afd6f256f: Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance. n5306fe4f73d1: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to train agents that adapt quickly to unseen tasks from limited interaction, but this requires representing task evidence over long interaction histories. n0482e6ea24f6: Nonparametric estimation of joint probability distributions is a core problem in statistics, which is notoriously challenging with high-dimensional data. When the conditional estimators adapt to sparsity in their conditioning sets, we characterize this difficulty through variable elimination in an undirected dependence graph. n5ab0404afbf8: On-policy distillation has been widely adopted for alleviating the distribution mismatch of off-policy distillation. In particular, using two coupled views of the same training example may strengthen its memorization. OP-Print builds on our finding that the supervision imprint in on-policy self-distillation is sparse and structured, concentrating on uncertainty-sensitive correction sites rather than across the entire rollout. Exploiting this property, we construct attack signals tailored to the two access levels: in the gray-box setting, OP-Print directly aggregates the privileged teacher-student residual correction along the same rollout; in the black-box setting, it measures restart-based output-basin stability as an observable surrogate for the hidden correction process. Across diverse models and distillation schemes, all baseline attacks remain essentially at random guessing even under gray-box access, whereas OP-Print is broadly validated to be effective in both gray-box and black-box settings.
nd5963ab40290: Recent methods for injecting graph structure into LLM prompts include graph soft prompting, in which a graph neural network (GNN) learns graph-specific tokens that capture relational information among entities in textual prompts. We provide evidence that the same failure is inherited by subsequent methods, even with multi-token pooling. We also examine conditions linked to this collapse and propose a two-stage procedure that yields non-collapsed tokens while maintaining competitive performance in most cases. However, token variability alone does not prove that the model uses graph information: via interventions and decoding probes, we show that depending on the configuration, a token can reflect the question, an answer prior, or graph-derived content that the LLM may or may not use. Code to reproduce our experiments is available at https://github.com/difra100/Token_Collapse_KGQA.
necc73ba0781e: Machine learning has permeated material optimization, providing high value. Pythia utilizes two of the most powerful machine learning concepts, foundational models and transfer learning. We employ a complex foundational model trained on a large dataset of chemically similar molecules, on a target that is physically close to our prediction target. Then, we freeze the weights and perform subspace alignment with the use of a transformer layer and add uncertainty quantification with gaussian processes. These two layers can be trained on a limited dataset yet allow us to leverage the gained knowl- edge and the studied materials and complex architectures. The resulting model is used as a surrogate for a Bayesian Optimization scheme. To showcase the robustness of the framework, we applied it to the investigation of adsorption and defect optimization of two distinct systems. Not only were we able to correctly and efficiently identify the optimal adsorption sites of even complex a
n7b87acc2c6a9: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent $α>1$ and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared $L_2$ approximation rate $\mathcal{O}((κ_P\log(m/δ)/m)^α)$ for two-layer networks of width $m$ and trainable proportion $P$, where $κ_P=(P/κ_1^*+(1-P)/κ_0^*)^{-1}$. The bound holds uniformly over the unit ball of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with probability at least $1-δ$. The constants $κ_0^*$ and $κ_1^*$ quantify the fixed and trainable groups' sampling mismatches relative to the target RKHS. For spherical biased-ReLU features in dimension $d$, we verify these assumptions with $α=(d+2)/(d-1)$ and $κ_0^*=4\sqrt{2}τ(d+1)/d$ for initialization scale $τ\ge1$, and $κ_1^*=1$ under ridge leverage sampling. For $d=5$ and $τ=10$, a trainable proportion of approximately $4.1\%$ captures $90\%$ of the reduction in the approximation bound from $P=0$ to $P=1$. A structured three-layer example illustrates how a few trainable first-layer neurons exploit fixed downstream blocks through nonlinear composition. Numerical experiments across diverse settings, including networks with up to 15 layers, exhibit similar phase transitions in training errors.
nf4f939a84f0f: We introduce Piano2Pop, a music-expansion task that transforms piano MIDI into instrumental pop productions. Enabled by recent advances in music generation and polyphonic music transcription, our pseudo-supervised approach conditions a pretrained flow-matching model on piano rolls without aligned piano-pop supervision. We train on synthetic piano-instrumental pairs derived from pop recordings, comparing pair-free transcription, including function-selective (FST) and register-density (RDA) augmentations, with a pair-supervised piano-cover generator as pseudo-demo sources. On 476 testing real-world piano-cover/pop pairs, the pair-supervised approach achieves the best Frechet Audio Distance, Accompaniment Prompt Adherence, and spectral shape on real-piano inputs, while FST mitigates piano-heavy outputs in pair-free training and remains a promising alternative. All fine-tuned systems significantly outperform the zero-shot baselines, which suggests a role for task-specific modeling.
n4448ef399605: Instrumental convergence is often invoked as a general reason to expect capable agents to acquire or express power-seeking subgoals: self-preservation, resource acquisition, deception, or resistance to oversight which poses an important threat to the society. Does reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) make a model more likely to express instrumental-convergence behavior, or does this depend on the training regime, evaluation frame, and stage of post-training? We study this question as a checkpoint-conditioned behavioral trajectory rather than as a single before/after safety score. The trajectory is nonmonotonic: instrumental rate rises from 25.0% at SFT to 46.1% near RLVR step 200, then falls to 11.8% at the final checkpoint. Paired item-level tests and step-wise regression support the final SFT-to-RLVR reduction. Prompt framing does not explain this pattern: a harmful-prompt indicator combined with other framing effects explains only 15% of within-checkpoint score variance on average, and Iterative Null-space Projection (INLP) removes a detectable framing direction without changing the SFT-to-final-RLVR gap. Together with preliminary 32B endpoint results (35.53% SFT to 22.37% RLVR final), these findings indicate that RLVR does not monotonically increase instrumental behavior in this setting: the rate rises early, then falls below the SFT baseline. The result is specific to this model family and benchmark, and judge agreement is moderate, so absolute rates should be read cautiously.
ncbdc0eb31c1e: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. Based on this information, we must decide whether to accept the AI decision automatically or consult an expert, such as a human auditor, who reviews the proposal and either accepts or corrects it. We formulate this task as an online constrained optimization problem in which the goal is to minimize the frequency of expert auditing while guaranteeing that the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited stays below a user-defined threshold. We derive a family of algorithms with provable error-control guarantees with no assumptions, including a method that is optimally efficient: it asymptotically attains the best achievable auditing rate for both adversarial and i.i.d. data streams. Experiments on screening harmful requests to large language models, qualitative text annotation, and data labeling show that our methods achieve valid error control in practice while substantially reducing the need for human auditing compared to baselines.
nbd042104fafe: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming. Importantly, the regression problem is learned end-to-end via backpropagation, while its coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass. This leads to TTR-Compressor, a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression. We evaluate TTR-Compressor as the compressor for block-wise sparse attention and the visual token merger for multimodal large language models. On block-wise sparse attention, TTR-Compressor improves RULER performance over attention-based compressors by a large margin. For visual token merging, it consistently outperforms the standard MLP merger and matches its performance with 55.6% fewer visual tokens. These results establish test-time regression as an effective primitive for sequence compression in efficient language and multimodal models.
n93b018684a95: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive.
